package_info.why_malicious: The package contains multiple critical vulnerabilities, including unauthenticated and authenticated OS command injection and privilege escalation, allowing attackers to execute arbitrary commands as root, leading to full system compromise.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code takes user-supplied input from the 'iface' GET parameter, concatenates it into a shell command, and executes it, allowing arbitrary command execution if special characters are injected.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Directly concatenating unsanitized user input into a shell command enables command injection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would sanitize or strictly validate input before using it in shell commands; here, user input is used unsafely.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would involve reading configuration files based on validated interface names.
key_indicators: Unsanitized user input in shell command
No authentication or CSRF protection for GET endpoint

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code takes the 'interface' POST parameter, concatenates it into a shell command, and executes it, allowing authenticated users to inject arbitrary commands.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: User input is directly inserted into a shell command without sanitization, enabling command injection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would validate or sanitize interface names before use in shell commands.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would be to query wireless interface names, but only after strict validation.
key_indicators: Direct use of POST parameter in shell command

execution_context.trigger: runtime (HTTP POST request, authenticated, triggered by QR code generation)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When generating a WiFi QR code, the code reads the SSID and password from the config file, which can contain shell injection payloads (e.g., $(touch /tmp/555)), resulting in arbitrary command execution when the QR code is generated.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The application fails to sanitize special characters in SSID and password fields, allowing shell command injection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would escape or reject special characters in configuration fields used in shell commands.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would be to generate QR codes for WiFi credentials, not to execute shell commands.
key_indicators: Special characters ($, (, )) allowed in config fields
Shell command execution via QR code generation

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the package configures sudoers to allow the web server user (www-data) to execute specific scripts as root without a password. If these scripts are writable by www-data, an attacker can modify them and escalate privileges to root.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Granting passwordless sudo access to scripts writable by a low-privileged user enables privilege escalation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would restrict sudo access to root-owned, non-writable scripts.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would be to allow controlled service management, but only with secure, root-owned scripts.

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a crafted GET request to /ajax/networking/get_netcfg.php with command injection payload in 'iface' parameter.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary command execution as www-data user.

attack_chain.action: Attacker leverages www-data access to modify writable scripts listed in sudoers (e.g., /etc/raspap/lighttpd/configport.sh).
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is inserted into a script that can be executed as root.

attack_chain.action: Attacker triggers execution of the modified script via sudo, escalating privileges to root.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full root compromise of the system.

attack_chain.action: Alternatively, an authenticated attacker injects commands via POST to /hostapd_conf or via SSID/password fields, which are executed during AP configuration or QR code generation.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary command execution as www-data, which can be chained with privilege escalation.

behavioral_signatures: Unsanitized user input in shell command execution
Passwordless sudo access for web server user
Modification and execution of writable scripts with root privileges
Creation of unexpected files (e.g., /tmp/555, /tmp/checkinterface) via web requests
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP requests to attacker-controlled IPs triggered by web requests
Unexpected connections from www-data or root to external hosts
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for web requests to /ajax/networking/get_netcfg.php or /hostapd_conf with suspicious parameters (e.g., containing shell metacharacters). Audit sudoers files for passwordless entries for www-data and check permissions of referenced scripts. Monitor for creation of suspicious files in /tmp and for outbound network connections initiated by www-data or root processes. Alert on modification of scripts in /etc/raspap by non-root users.
